summary: A contract can make a tool legible without making its implementation correct, secure or easy for a model to use.

points.text: JSON Schema describes shape, not the full semantics of side effects, race conditions or domain invariants; executable contract tests and runtime policy remain necessary.
Too many tiny operations create long plans and partial-failure states, while one giant operation hides control. The interface needs task-shaped granularity, not maximal decomposition.
Versioning contracts and maintaining adapters adds cost, especially when upstream CLIs or web interfaces change without machine-readable compatibility guarantees.
